h: חַג הַפֶּסַח, מַאֲמָר ל״ד Pesach — Maamar Lamed Daled
Love Without Reason, Joy Through Deeds: Shabbos, Yom Tov and Pesach

"Is not Esav a brother to Yaakov?"
that is, their deeds are equal,
and even if Yaakov, Heaven forbid,
acts like the deeds of Esav,
or Esav acts like the deeds of Yaakov,
that is, he is truly worthy of love
in the manner of what is said
"My son, if your heart is wise,
whom, out of Your love with which You loved him
and Your joy with which You rejoiced in him";
love from His will, may He be blessed, without reason,
and "Your joy with which You rejoiced in him,"
that is, on account of his favorable deeds,
by reason of which he is worthy of love.
that is, from love without reason.

"Even though he sinned, he is Yisrael";
so that of his seed, even if one's sins grow
כְּמוֹ שֶׁחָשְׁבוּ שָׁם בַּגְּמָרָא עַל עָכָן,
as they reckoned there in the Gemara regarding Achan,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם לֹא יֹאבַד שְׁמוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל.
nevertheless his name Yisrael will not be lost.
from the side of Hashem, may He be blessed,

and I wish to give it to Israel"

"it is a sign between Me and you,"

Nevertheless we say: "You have bequeathed us,"
to bring holiness into the times,
is from Hashem, may He be blessed,
שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא קִידֵּשׁ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
for the Holy One, blessed be He, sanctified Israel,
'And you shall be holy to Me, etc.';
and since they are sanctified to Heaven,
לְכָךְ מַה שֶּׁהֵם מְקַדְּשִׁים הוּא מְקוּדָּשׁ.
therefore what they sanctify is sanctified.
Go and learn from the service vessels," etc.
And in all the festivals there is
מִצְוַת שִׂמְחָה מִצַּד צִיוּוּי ה' יִתְבָּרֵךְ,
a mitzvah of joy by the command of Hashem, may He be blessed;
which has no mitzvah of joy;
"'And on the day of your rejoicing' — these are the Shabbosos."
For on Shabbos there is no mitzvah of joy,
only that the Jew rejoices in it from his own side,
"Those who keep Shabbos will rejoice in Your kingship."
And this is through the holiness
that Hashem, may He be blessed, places in the heart of Israel,
וְזוֹכֶה עַל יְדֵי זֶה לְיַשְׁרוּת הַלֵּב,
and through this one merits uprightness of heart,
as brought in the holy Zohar
"For their generations (ledorosam)" — one who makes them a dwelling (dirah) on Shabbos
in the two chambers of the heart,
and the evil inclination is cleared away from there, etc.;
that is, to empty out the evil
from the foolish heart as well.
And when one merits uprightness of heart,
"And for the upright of heart, joy"
נִזְכַּר בּוֹ כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים מִצְוַת שִׂמְחָה,
the mitzvah of joy is mentioned several times,
and likewise on Shavuos the mitzvah of joy is written;
the mitzvah of joy is not written explicitly,
but is learned from Sukkos and Shavuos.
וּבְכָל חַג יֵשׁ בּוֹ בִּרְכַּת הֶחָג,
And every festival has the blessing of the festival,
"And bestow upon us, Hashem our God,
And regarding Sukkos is written explicitly
a blessing in matters of this world,
"For Hashem your God will bless you
in all your produce and in all the work of your hands";
and regarding Shavuos too it is written
"The measure of the freewill offering of your hand, etc.,
as Hashem your God will bless you";
And the mitzvah of joy is through eating and drinking,
"There is no joy except with meat;
there is no joy except with wine."
And on Pesach the mitzvah comes through eating,
yet no mitzvah of joy is mentioned for it;
for in truth on Pesach too
the essence of the holiness was from Hashem, may He be blessed,
for the essence of the Exodus was
only from the side of Hashem, may He be blessed;
and as we said, for this reason
נִקְרָא חַג הַפֶּסַח בַּתּוֹרָה בְּשֵׁם שַׁבָּת:
Chag HaPesach is called "Shabbos" in the Torah:
But since the mitzvah of eating matzah
is that there be no leaven in it,
that is, that there be found in the eating
and that it be an eating in holiness —
אֲזַי מִמֵּילָא יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִצְוַת שִׂמְחָה,
then as a matter of course there is in it a mitzvah of joy,
for one merits uprightness of heart,
and "for the upright of heart, joy."
Nevertheless, on Pesach too we say:
"with joy and with gladness You have bequeathed us,"
for the mitzvah is from Israel's side,
so that no leaven be found in it,
which is "the leaven in the dough,"
וְנִלְמָד בּוֹ מִצְוַת שִׂמְחָה גַּם כֵּן.
and the mitzvah of joy is learned for it as well.
And likewise it has the blessing of the festival
also in matters of this world,
"Bring before Me the Omer on Pesach,
so that there be blessed for you
And on Shabbos that is Yom Tov we say:
with joy and with gladness You have bequeathed us";
for "with love and with favor" refers
וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא
And this is in the manner of what they said in the Gemara
"Does Shabbos then avail for the Mussaf offerings,
and not avail for the daily offerings?"
For the daily offering on Shabbos
has some of the holiness of Shabbos.
avail for its own Mussaf offerings,
and not avail for the Mussaf offerings of Shabbos?"
דְּמוּסְפֵי שַׁבָּת שֶׁחָל בּוֹ רֹאשׁ חוֹדֶשׁ
For the Shabbos Mussaf on which Rosh Chodesh falls
has some of the holiness of Rosh Chodesh.
And likewise: "Does Rosh Hashanah then," etc.,
"not avail for the Mussaf offerings of Rosh Chodesh?"
"not avail for the blessing over wine?"
Even though the blessing "Who creates the fruit of the vine"
מִכָּל מָקוֹם בִּרְכַּת בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי הַגֶּפֶן
nevertheless the blessing "Who creates the fruit of the vine"
recited over the wine of Kiddush

for the holiness of Yom Tov,
so that even the holiness of Yom Tov

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Chaim Chaikel of Amdur, Chaim VaChesed 492 — “‘These are the appointed times of Hashem, which you shall call holy convocations’: these are My appointed times, for we give delight to Hashem and adorn Him, as it were. ‘Which you shall call in their appointed time’: through your adornment, that is, through your service, so that you draw His bounty to yourselves. Therefore on Shabbos we say ‘with love and with favor,’ and on Yom Tov ‘with joy and with gladness,’ for on Yom Tov we bring Him delight from our service, and so on Yom Tov one must let the poor benefit from his meal; whereas on Shabbos the Holy One brings delight to us.” Connection: The same distinction is drawn from the same liturgical words: Shabbos flows from Above, Yom Tov is drawn down through Israel's service; R. Chaim Chaikel adds a halachic expression of it, the duty to include the poor in the Yom Tov meal.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Beis Yaakov, Bereishis, Noach 13 — “And in this way it is also with the holiness of Yom Tov: it appears to human eyes that Israel sanctifies it, as it says in Rosh Hashanah 24a, ‘which you shall call them’ — read it ‘you.’ But in truth, at the root it is a fixed and established holiness like the holiness of Shabbos; only because the Holy One, blessed be He, wished to let His people taste the taste of the toil of their own hands is this holiness called by their name.” Connection: Like the maamar’s “You have bequeathed us,” it traces Israel’s power to sanctify Yom Tov back to Hashem; it goes further, holding that the festival’s holiness is at root as fixed as Shabbos and is credited to Israel so they may taste the fruit of their own labor.

paragraphs.text: Zevachim 91a — "Even though the Mussafin are holier — does Shabbos avail for the Mussafin and not avail for the Temidin?" And: "Does Rosh Chodesh avail for its own Mussafin and not avail for the Mussafin of Shabbos?" Rashi: the Mussafin bear the name of Shabbos; but since the Temidin are offered today, the name of Shabbos is on them too.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Av 2 — “In the Gemara (Zevachim) it concludes: ‘Does Rosh Chodesh then avail for its own Mussaf offerings and not avail for the Mussaf offerings of Shabbos?’ That is, when Rosh Chodesh falls on Shabbos, Rosh Chodesh avails so that the holiness of Shabbos too is reckoned as ‘his own kav.’ For in truth on Shabbos too it is written ‘Remember the Shabbos day to sanctify it’… Yet the essence of the holiness of Shabbos is from Hashem’s side; but when Rosh Chodesh falls on Shabbos, it avails for the added holiness of Shabbos too, that it also be called by Israel’s name.” Connection: The same reading of Zevachim 91a, applied to Rosh Chodesh; it adds that the holiness Israel brings is “his own kav,” which a person prefers to nine kavin of his fellow (Bava Metzia 38a).
